title: Analytics API queries
lead: Run fixed local aggregates or Query API requests with explicit periods and breakdowns. Configure credentials on the server; public Pages has no aggregate-query server.

items: Configure the local Web development server with the Analytics license to inspect and an API key, then start it.
Open Bitmovin Analytics (server-proxied query) and select one of four fixed aggregates. See Choose an Analytics metric for definitions.
After Querying… finishes, read the selected preset, result-row count and values. Durations remain in milliseconds.
Each click aggregates the preceding 7 days. The panel has no date or category selector, charts or free-form query input.

items.label: Definitions of the four query presets

rows: Allows player usage for an authorized host/app
Player configuration; it is not the Query API secret.
Selects the collector destination and queried dataset
Server-only BITMOVIN_ANALYTICS_API_KEY, or the BITMOVIN_API_KEY fallback.
Selects an authorized organization for the API key

blocks.text: Replace placeholders only in local/server settings and restart the development server. Keep account API keys out of VITE_*, Player Config, source URLs and client code. Static Pages has no server to hold secrets.
Read the result and JSON response

The panel displays result rows. /api/analytics/query returns those rows, their count, and the requested aggregation and dimension. This invented example returns a count of 42; rowCount: 1 is the result-row count, not the impression count.

Without interval or groupBy, a count normally occupies one value in one row. Empty results display (no rows). A successful response does not establish that the intended source, license, period or filters matched data.
Call the local proxy from your terminal to specify a UTC range. Use your development server’s port; the example uses 5173. The server supplies the license and API key, so the request omits them.
Use the Query API for a breakdown

This example averages VIDEO_STARTUPTIME > 0 by browser and hour. Save the JSON as query.json, replace the Analytics license and choose dates within data retention. Run it from a server or terminal rather than the local GUI.

blocks.title: Send from your server or trusted terminal

blocks.text: Use a BITMOVIN_API_KEY authorized to read the data, adding X-Tenant-Org-Id only when required. API results appear in data.result and may include columnLabels or contextDescription; use those labels to identify columns. The app proxy returns rows and rowCount and does not support every response field or option.
Keep the same population when comparing

items: start and end define the whole period. Use UTC timestamps within data retention.
interval defines MINUTE, HOUR, DAY or MONTH buckets, rather than the overall period.
groupBy selects categories such as BROWSER, COUNTRY, DEVICE_TYPE or OPERATINGSYSTEM. filters restricts the data, for example BROWSER EQ Chrome or VIDEO_STARTUPTIME GT 0.
Keep the license, range, time zone, conditions, aggregation, units and collector coverage with results. Not every collector reports every field.

blocks.text: If a query does not return the expected value

rows: The server lacks an Analytics license or API secret. Configure the server, rather than entering a secret in the browser.
Check JSON syntax, aggregation, dimension and ISO-8601 start/end fields.
Check the server API key's permissions and organization scope; a Player license cannot authenticate this API.
Check that the development backend can reach the upstream API. A static build alone has no proxy.
Check the selected Analytics license, collected data, range and filters before interpreting it as a zero result.
